concerns.text: The plan assumes that intrinsic properties (dependency_depth, semantic_scope, syntactic_complexity) are available for *all* code instances, yet only the synthetic generator explicitly provides these values. Real TIDE instances have no measured dependency depth or semantic scope, so the construct validity of these predictors is compromised. The methodology must either extract comparable metrics from real code or acknowledge the mismatch.

Power analysis is deferred to a generic GofPower call without specifying effect size, predictor count, or variance assumptions. With ~400 total instances (200 real + 200 synthetic) and six predictors, achieving ≥80 % power to detect an odds‑ratio of 1.5 may be optimistic. Provide a concrete power calculation (e.g., required N) or increase sample size.

Including `origin` (real vs. synthetic) as a covariate may not fully control for systematic differences between the two data sources. Because synthetic instances are generated to span the full range of the three intrinsic properties, their feature distribution will differ from real data, potentially confounding the relationship between predictors and static detection success. Consider stratified analyses or separate models for each origin.

The marginal threshold estimation fixes all other predictors at their training‑set means and searches for the value where predicted probability = 0.5. This assumes additive, independent effects and ignores interactions among predictors, which may lead to misleading “complexity thresholds”. A more robust approach would report marginal effects from the full model (e.g., partial dependence) or explore interaction terms.

The checklist states that no causal claims are made, yet the research objective phrasing (“determine which intrinsic code properties constitute the complexity threshold where the deterministic static detector drops below a 0.5 probability”) can be interpreted as implying a causal boundary. Clarify that the analysis is correlational and avoid language that suggests causation.
